name: Nino Konis Santana National Park
blurb: Monsoon forest, lake and reef at the eastern tip of Timor.

tip.title: Lose the fig trees
tip.text: Figs feed monkeys, bats, doves and deer. Reduce the variegated fig and watch fruit eaters decline, then the pythons that eat them.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Nino Konis Santana National Park
Tatoli: Timor's native deer in desperate bid for survival

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Timor deer
nodes.desc: Native deer eating grass, leaves and fallen fruit. It is listed as vulnerable, and dry-season water shortages have killed deer on Jaco Island.

nodes.name: Crab-eating macaque
nodes.desc: An omnivorous monkey recorded in the park area. It eats fruit such as figs and Antidesma, and also insects.
A small introduced rodent that eats seeds, fruit and insects. It is food for snakes and other predators.

nodes.name: Four-lined tree frog
nodes.desc: A tree frog that eats insects. It is prey for snakes such as the white-lipped island pitviper, according to GloBI.
An opportunistic top predator of coasts and rivers that takes deer and many other animals. It is considered holy on Timor.
Strong year-round sun lets the forest and grassland plants grow all year when water is available.
Rain comes mostly in a wet season. When the rains fail, as in late 2019, water points dry up and deer suffer.
Soil on limestone terraces and lowland ground that holds the nutrients and water plants draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil life
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
